criteria.name: artwork_craft
criteria.why: Some frames are strong. Slide 6 is the best image in the deck: a black anodised tray with three channels, a cleaved half disc and hex screws. Twelve against four and a half against nineteen, with the November channel left open, reads at feed size with no text. Slides 3 and 4 put a capped boat in a pool of light on a dark field, as the brief asks. The weak frames fall below the 7 descriptor. Slide 7 is a small copper scrap, about 15 percent of the frame, on diagonal grooves. At 432 px it does not read as a crystal growth surface or as islands that have not joined, and nothing owns the frame. Slide 8's seated person is a lumpy primitive head with no shoulders. The black nineteen-wafer boat beside the laptop reads as a heater, not as wafers. Slide 2 is a textured terracotta square in a grid. Only a reader who knows the Panhandle's square counties reads it as Lubbock County, and the 'Lubbock County' label sits in the footer band between 'c3 c18 c19' and the site line. Slide 9 is type set into recessed plates on a steel nameplate. The empty IN SERVICE field is a good idea, but the descriptor names type on plates as a 4 trait. On slide 5 the cleaved half is a flat grey wedge that a reader cannot tell is half a wafer.

criteria.name: deck_coherence
criteria.why: The wafer boat at one pitch carries slides 1, 3, 4, 5, 6 and 8, and a reader can describe the spine unprompted: one wafer stands for $1 million. The dusk_gold accent means only the November award, which the storyboard declares and slides 1, 2, 6 and 9 honour. The value stays dark across the contact sheet with no strobe. The three plan-view reliefs (2, 7, 9) leave the lit bench for flat orthographic material, though, and slides 2 and 7 sit outside the deck's object world. Slide 8's office desk is a third register. That is one deck with a working motif and more than one frame slightly outside it.

criteria.name: claim_integrity
criteria.why: Every printed numeral traces to claims.json or figures.json. $19M is c1 and nov_floor_m. $12M is c15. $24M is c16. $4.5M is c17. 2023 is c19. 'Three awards' is awards_2026 from c15, c17 and c1. The wafer counts are drawing units declared in figures.json. The deck handles inexact figures with real care: slide 6 says 'over' is a floor and 'roughly' is roughly, and draws no total. Every source is a primary Texas Tech page that was fetched. Two looser points. The cover's 'a cluster not built yet' rests on c4, whose quote is only 'will help Texas Tech establish', so 'not built' is an inference from the verb. Second, all three sources are the university's own releases about itself. The CHIPS Office listing is off limits and the deck says so, but no award figure is confirmed by the body that made the award. Unprinted: c9 says Faller 'leads' the team, which its quote does not support.

criteria.name: story_and_stakes
criteria.why: A Texan learns what happened (a third award from the state chip fund, over $19M, toward a computing cluster), where (Lubbock, Lubbock County on slide 2) and through whom (the Texas CHIPS Office in the Office of the Governor, slide 2). The descriptor's 10 needs a deadline and something the reader can do next, and the deck has neither. There is no meeting, no comment window and no named place to watch. The close's only call is the caption's 'When does Texas Tech put a date on it?'. The stake is never made concrete for a person in Lubbock or anywhere else in Texas: who will use the cluster and what it changes. Slide 7 says the purpose in the university's words, not the reader's. One more problem: a reader seeing 'chip fund' pay for 'Nvidia chips' on slide 8 is not told why a semiconductor fund buys a computing cluster until the dense body copy on slide 7. This is a clear topic with a soft stake.

criteria.name: sequence_and_momentum
criteria.why: The cover earns the swipe ('Over $19 million for a cluster not built yet'), and the close lands on slide 9's empty IN SERVICE plate. Frame 2 does not pay at once. It turns to governance ('by way of the governor's office') before the reader has the story. Slides 3, 4 and 5 are three frames of earlier-award history that slide 6 then recaps whole. Slide 4, the match, could fold into slide 3 without loss. There is no real turn where understanding changes. The deck explains, then closes on the absence it opened with.

criteria.name: voice
criteria.why: The copy is clean and on register, and it observes the house rules: no colons, ordinal dates, no year on November 13th, no banned word as a whole word. 'Three awards, three kinds of number' is the best line in the deck. But 'Drawn to illustrate' or a variant closes eight of nine deks, and the cover spends its dek on 'The boat is drawn to illustrate and has no far end', which is a disclaimer, not a sentence a Texan wants. Slide 7 quotes press-release diction ('high-fidelity simulation data', 'shorten development cycles'). There is little regional specificity beyond the word Lubbock. Nothing says what the South Plains gets or why Lubbock. Note for integrity: slide 5's paraphrase 'ultrawide bandgap' contains the banned string 'gap' inside a compound word. word_ban almost certainly uses word boundaries, so I do not count it as a fail, but the paraphrase could avoid it as the caption did ('meant for harsh environments').

criteria.name: variety
criteria.why: Nothing repeats inside the 30-day window. No earlier deck covers this Texas Tech award or the fund. The angle and the opening move are familiar, though. No. 65 on November 1st was a university AI facility grant whose refusals were 'any opening date', and no. 69 on November 5th was capacity announced against a building not ready. 'Money announced, no date for the thing' is the third such opening in two weeks. The drawing-unit device (one object per counted unit, stated in the dek) has driven nos. 66 to 76 and is now the house habit, not a fresh technique. The palette of dark lab, cold flood and one dusk_gold accent is close to nos. 73 and 76.

one_sentence_fix: Fold slide 4 into slide 3. Use the freed frame, and slide 2's abstract county square, to put a concrete Texas stake on screen from the claims already held: who in Lubbock gets to use the cluster and for what (c6, c10, c12), plus the one thing a reader can watch for. As it stands, a Texan finishes the deck knowing the size of the money and nothing about what it changes for them.

artwork_weakest_frames.problem: A small copper scrap fills about 15 percent of the frame on grooved dark terraces. At 432 px it reads as a torn piece of foil, not as a growth surface with unjoined islands, and nothing owns the frame.
artwork_weakest_frames.fix: Raise the relief camera to fill the lower 60 percent with three or four lit terrace risers running off both edges. Model the top layer as a dozen separate raised copper islands with lit edges and cast shadows across one terrace, so the half-grown layer is the dominant silhouette.

artwork_weakest_frames.problem: The seated person is a lumpy primitive head with no shoulders in the lower-left corner, and the black boat of nineteen wafers reads as a space heater beside the laptop.
artwork_weakest_frames.fix: Drop the person and reframe on the boat. Put the mirror-silicon wafers from slides 1 and 3 in the near third with the warm strip behind them, so the rims catch light and read as wafers. Keep the laptop behind as the scale reference.

artwork_weakest_frames.problem: A flat textured square in a grid that only reads as Lubbock County with its label, and the 'Lubbock County' label is set in the footer band between the cite and the site line.
artwork_weakest_frames.fix: Lower the county grid and light it raking from the deck's -58 azimuth so the raised Lubbock County block casts a long shadow onto its neighbours. Move the county label up onto the block itself, clear of the footer row.

artwork_weakest_frames.problem: The close is type set into recessed plates on a nameplate, which reads as UI and is the descriptor's 'type on plates' trait.
artwork_weakest_frames.fix: Keep the empty IN SERVICE field. Make the hero the open November boat with no far end plate, sitting below a smaller nameplate, so the closing image is the deck's object, not three text boxes.

artwork_weakest_frames.problem: The cleaved half is a flat grey wedge in front of four mirror discs, so at feed size it does not read as half a wafer.
artwork_weakest_frames.fix: Pull the camera back to a three-quarter view so the half wafer's D outline and its lit straight cleave face show in full beside the four whole discs.
